critical_code_review_comments: POST /reports weather is properly bounded by asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=6.0) and the except catches both TimeoutError and generic Exception → weather=None fallback works and does not block the response. Confirmed by wall-clock timing (<10s) with empty adres. Good defensive pattern.

Element uniqueness is enforced both at application-layer (409 in create_element/update_element) AND at the Mongo partial-unique index level (uniq_element_kod). Two-tier defense is correct: index survives races that the app-level check might miss.

GET /reports/{id} now enriches with klient_nazwa/elementy/extra_godziny by doing N+1 lookups per element and per extra hour row. For reports with many elements/extras this could be N queries — acceptable for typical daily reports (<20 elements) but consider $lookup aggregation if reports grow. Not a blocker.

POST /issues explicitly returns 403 when user['rola']=='contractor' BEFORE any DB work. Clean short-circuit. However the endpoint uses generic current_user dep — a contractor could still receive 401 vs 403 based on token expiration; that's OK. Verified 403 in test.

POST /auth/change-password uses must_change_password to skip old-password verification, which matches product intent for forced-rotation. Old password re-login is correctly rejected (verified in test).

strip_project_financials is applied on list_projects + get_project but NOT on PUT /projects/{id} responses. PUT is admin-only today so no leak, but defensive uniformity would prevent future regressions if scope widens. (Same note as iter_6.)
